newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: MAIN PLAYERS IN REPUBLIC DEBATE WELCOME FISCHER
The National Party has entered the debate on the Constitutional Future of Australia, announcing options it could take if there's overwhelming public support for a republic.
Party Leader Tim Fischer says although his party remains committed to a constitutional monarchy, it's considering a minimalist republic model as an option.
He says one option is to empower the High Court Chief Justice to appoint the governor-general on the Prime Minister's advice.
Chairman of the Australian Republican Movement, Malcolm Turnbull, describes the model as insufficiently democratic, but he's welcomed discussion by the Nationals on the issue.
Executive Director of Australians for a Constitutional Monarchy, Kerry Jones also welcomed Mr Fischer's entry into the debate, but says his plan can't work.
She says any model of appointment will set a political precedent.
TAX EXPERTS SAY INDIVIDUALS SLUGGED AND COMPANIES NOT
The Tax and Accountants Association says new industrial relations packages may put many people into higher tax brackets, reducing the value of the rise.
President Ray Regan says that's not fair, especially when people earning more than 50-thousand dollars a year pay 35-per-cent more tax than companies.
Mr Regan says individuals are losing almost 50 per cent of their earnings in tax once they pass the 50-thousand dollar threshold.
He says the government doesn't seem to care about slugging individuals, while it's giving companies a competitive tax rate of 36 per cent.
FUNDING CUTS PROPOSED IF RECOMMENDATIONS NOT IMPLEMENTED
The Federal Government is being urged to cut funding to states which don't fully implement the recommendations of the Black Deaths in Custody Royal Commission.
The Australian Council for Civil Liberties President, Terry O'Gorman says Aboriginal Affairs Minister, John Herron should take a stand at this year's Commonwealth Summit on the issue.
Mr O'Gorman, says the Summit will allow the States to report on their progress.
And he says if they've failed to implement the recommendations of the 1991 Inquiry, they should be penalised.
NEW RACQUET GIVES HINGIS POWER BOOST
At the Hopman Cup tennis tournament in Perth, Switzerland's Martina Hingis says a new racquet is giving her game a power boost.
The 16 year-old, who blasted South Africa's Amanda Coetzer off the court yesterday, 6-1, 6-2, says her new racquet is five centimetres longer than she's used to playing with.
Hingis says she's hitting the ball harder and with more power than ever before.
ECSTASY DEATH HAS ADELAIDE POLICE WORRIED
Police in Adelaide are concerned about anyone who's taken ecstasy or similar synthetic drugs recently, after the death of a 26 year-old woman in the Flinders Medical Centre last night.
It's believed the woman took the drug on New Year's Eve. Police say she may have taken the designer drug at a city nightclub, or later at a party at Mitchell Park.
They're worried others who were with her may have taken the same drugs, and may be needing urgent medical attention.
If post mortem tests confirm the woman had taken ecstasy, she'll be the fourth person in South Australia to have died from the drug in 12 months.
